title: Method for detecting and quantitating capture of organic molecules in hypervelocity impacts
author: Kazemi, New, et al.
materials: The major steps in the method include preparing PB solutions at various concentrations and depositing PB droplets of known small volume onto an aluminum substrate. After dehydrating the droplets, the sample was inserted into the humidification apparatus equipped with an epifluorescence microscope, an oblique white light illumination system and a CCD camera. The sample was then humidified to a humidity determined to make the PB strongly fluorescent. Then the integrated fluorescence intensity of the spot was measured to determine the fluorescence intensity per Pacific Blue molecule on the surface.

Pacific Blue™ succinimidyl ester (PB), purchased from ThermoFisher Scientific, was dissolved in DMF (dimethylformamide) to produce a 10 mM stock solution. Serial dilutions of the stock solution in 30 mM sodium tetraborate, pH 9.3 were performed to produce 10 µM, 1 µM, 100 nM, and 10 nM PB solutions. A 2-inch circle of cardboard covered with rubber silicone tape was used to create a soft substrate to support the aluminum foil for droplet deposition. Using a soft support substrate ensures that the tip of the syringe contacts and stays in contact with the surface and facilitates a complete transfer of droplet from the tip of the syringe onto the surface. Aluminum foil was placed shiny side down on the rubber tape and cleaned by gently rubbing with lens tissue wetted with acetone. This process also smoothed the surface of the foil. If the foil is cleaned too aggressively the increased surface hydrophobicity prevents the droplets from wetting the surface, whereas a somewhat hydrophilic surface enables reproducible droplet deposition with a uniform size when dehydrated.

steps.title: Prepare PB stock and dilutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve Pacific Blue™ succinimidyl ester (PB) in dimethylformamide (DMF) to make a 10 mM stock solution. Serially dilute this stock in 30 mM sodium tetraborate buffer (pH 9.3) to obtain working solutions of 10 µM, 1 µM, 100 nM, and 10 nM PB.

steps.title: Prepare aluminum substrate
steps.instruction: Cut a 2‑inch diameter circle of cardboard, cover it with rubber silicone tape, and place a piece of aluminum foil shiny‑side down on the tape. Gently rub the foil with lens tissue wetted with acetone to clean and slightly smooth the surface, avoiding aggressive rubbing that would make the surface too hydrophobic.

steps.title: Assemble spotter and load syringes
steps.instruction: Build the custom micro‑droplet spotter using three orthogonal linear stages and a 3‑D‑printed syringe holder that positions a syringe perpendicular to the foil with ~32 µm vertical accuracy. Load four 0.5 µL Hamilton 7000 Series point‑style 3 syringes—one for each PB concentration—and a fifth syringe containing only 30 mM sodium tetraborate buffer for blank controls.

steps.title: Deposit 10× calibration droplets
steps.instruction: Using the spotter, deposit 50 nL droplets of each PB concentration (10 µM, 1 µM, 100 nM, 10 nM) and a blank buffer onto the foil, three replicates per concentration, producing droplets of approximately 500 µm diameter.

steps.title: Deposit 20× calibration droplets
steps.instruction: Using the same spotter, deposit 5 nL droplets of each PB concentration and a blank, twenty‑four replicates per concentration, producing droplets of approximately 250 µm diameter.

steps.title: Dry deposited droplets
steps.instruction: Store the 10× and 20× droplet arrays in a dark room at ambient temperature for 24 h to allow complete dehydration, mimicking post‑impact drying.

steps.title: Determine optimal humidity
steps.instruction: Place three 1 µM PB droplets (dried 24 h) under the microscope shroud. Reduce chamber humidity to 10 % with dry nitrogen, then introduce humid nitrogen at 3.5 ± 0.1 L min⁻¹ while keeping water temperature at 38 ± 1 °C. Capture fluorescence images every 20 % increase in humidity from 10 % to 90 % with 1 s exposure. Identify the humidity at which fluorescence plateaus (70 %); avoid higher humidity that causes condensation.

steps.title: Re‑humidify samples to optimal level
steps.instruction: After drying, re‑humidify the calibration arrays to 70 % relative humidity using the same humid nitrogen flow before imaging.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Using the epifluorescence microscope and CCD camera, acquire images of each droplet with MediaCybernetics Image‑Pro‑Express software. Set exposure time to 10 s for 10 nM and 100 nM droplets, 1 s for 1 µM droplets, and 0.1 s for 10 µM droplets to avoid pixel saturation.

steps.title: Analyze images for integrated intensity
steps.instruction: Import each image into ImageJ via the Bio‑Formats Importer, split into RGB channels, and work on the blue channel. Define a Region of Interest (ROI) outlining the humidified droplet and five nearby background ROIs. Record the mean signal intensity (Īs) of the droplet ROI and the average background intensity (ĪB) from the five ROIs. Measure the droplet area (A) in µm² and compute integrated intensity using I = (Īs − ĪB) × A / s (s = exposure time in seconds). Calculate the amount of PB in picomoles as Picomoles = C × V × 10⁻³, where C is the PB concentration (µM) and V is the deposited volume (nL).
